prompt_text: Who is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City to help me pick a plan?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single “best” broker for everyone — the right broker depends on what kind of coverage you need (individual/family, small‑group, Medicare, Medicaid/CHIP), whether you’re on the Missouri or Kansas side of Kansas City, and what level of service you want (in‑person help, ongoing support, or just enrollment). I can help you find a great match — first, a few tips on how to choose one and an offer to look up options for your ZIP code.

How to find a good health insurance broker in Kansas City
- Define your need: individual/family ACA plan, employer group plan, Medicare, or short‑term? Brokers often specialize.
- Check licensing and credentials: use the Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance or the Kansas Insurance Department to verify an agent’s license. Look for NAHU (National Association of Health Underwriters) membership.
- Confirm carrier access: a good broker represents multiple insurers (not captive to one carrier), so they can compare plans across carriers.
- Ask about cost: brokers typically earn commissions from insurers; confirm whether they charge any fees and whether they’ll recommend plans based on your best interest or commissions.
- Look for experience with your situation: ask how many clients like you they serve (e.g., number of Medicare clients, ACA enrollments, small employers).
- Read reviews: Google, Yelp, and Better Business Bureau can show patterns of customer service and complaints.
- Availability and support: ask whether they provide year‑round help (claims, renewals, life changes) or only initial enrollment, and whether they do in‑person or virtual meetings.
- Ask for references: a good broker should provide references or testimonials.

Questions to ask a prospective broker
- Which carriers do you represent?
- Do you charge a fee? If not, how are you compensated?
- How much experience do you have with [ACA/Medicare/small group] plans?
- Can you help with claims and appeals? Do you provide year‑round support?
- Can you provide references from clients in Kansas City?
- Will you help me with subsidies eligibility and enrollment on the ACA marketplace (if applicable)?

Places to search
- NAHU “Find an Agent” directory
- Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance / Kansas Insurance Department license lookups
- Medicare.gov’s “Find a Medicare Plan” and local SHIP (State Health Insurance Assistance Program) for unbiased Medicare counseling
- Local Google/Yelp searches for “health insurance broker Kansas City” for customer reviews

If you want, I can:
- Look up brokers near you (I’ll need your ZIP code and whether you’re in Missouri or Kansas)
- Recommend 3–5 brokers/agents with solid reviews and the right specialty (individual vs. Medicare vs. small business)
Tell me which type of plan you need and your ZIP code and I’ll find some specific, relevant options.
